stories.title: Public hospitals lost millions over unpaid private bills
stories.summary: Public hospitals are losing millions of euro a year due to unpaid bills from private health insurers, new figures show. Over the last four years across HSE-run and voluntary hospitals, €125.1 million has been written off in private insurance claims. In that time, €37.6 million has been lost as a result of the HSE not properly submitting claims to insurers. Public hospitals routinely earn millions from fee-paying patients. However, procedures for private patients are seemingly carried out free of charge in the public system on a routine basis due to unpaid bills submitted to health insurers. This means the taxpayer rather than the insurer is footing the bill for treatments and comes with several hospitals under financial strain.

stories.title: Bitter exchanges in Dáil over Triple Lock legislation
stories.summary: There have been bitter exchanges in the Dáil this afternoon ahead of the Government bringing forward legislation tomorrow to amend the Triple Lock. Members of the Opposition held up signs while the Ceann Comhairle took to her feet to demand that they be put away. Verona Murphy warned members of Sinn Féin and People Before Profit that they were out of order for continuing to display the A4 pieces of paper, each of which read "save neutrality". After ringing her bell and standing up, they finally relented. Deputies then criticised the duration of the debate which is to be held over three hours later, demanding that it be continued in another session. People Before Profit TD Richard Boyd Barrett, Labour TD Duncan Smith and Sinn Féin TD Donnchadh Ó Laoghaire all voiced their opposition to the Government motion.

stories.title: Turnkey acquisitions for social housing to be phased out
stories.summary: The purchase of new turnkey properties for social housing is set to be phased out under plans that went before Cabinet this morning. Minister for Housing James Browne announced that funding for these acquisitions by local authorities and approved housing bodies will end late next year. This policy change is aiming to get local authorities to take a more hands-on approach to building social housing. Housing bodies and the Land Development Agency will have a major role too. Minister Browne has been critical of what he sees as a reliance by councils on buying homes that would otherwise be available on the private market. The minister also believes these purchases prevent councils and housing bodies from influencing the homes' design.

stories.title: Over third of businesses yet to model AI impact - Ibec
stories.summary: More than a third of employers have yet to model the impact of AI on their workforce, according to new research from business group Ibec. The latest Talent Trends Report shows that just 4% of businesses believe AI will lead to a significant reduction in overall headcount. The research found that 36% of respondents have yet to formally model the impact on workforce structures. The report also shows that 61% of HR leaders say their company does not plan to change its hybrid policies next year. Meanwhile, the implementation of the EU Pay Transparency Directive was identified as the single most impactful factor affecting HR operations, cited by 68% of HR leaders as compliance deadlines approach. Executive Director of Employer Relations at Ibec Maeve McElwee said there is genuine confidence that while some roles may be changed by AI, the narrative of job displacement does not currently reflect what HR leaders are seeing.

stories.title: France to deploy some military forces for weekend protest
stories.summary: France will deploy some military forces to reinforce police during protests planned for this coming Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. "We will deploy the Sentinelle force, obviously as a substitute to interior security forces ... mostly to free police and gendarmes in their mission to maintain order," Mr Nunez told the National Assembly. He was speaking after Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said police deployment for Saturday's demonstrations would be "massive" and that his goal was for an "immediate return to order" following a weekend of violent riots. It comes as the country said it will impose new curfews in areas where needed, Mr Lecornu said, adding that the measures introduced in several cities the previous day had "helped keep the night calm". Paris police ordered a new curfew for parts of the city tonight. The fresh curfew runs from 9pm to 4am and applies to the Republic public square in the city's central east, where many weekend clashes took place, and in the central les Halles district which is full of shops.

stories.title: Nankivell - 'International rugby is still the pinnacle'
stories.summary: Alex Nankivell has previously spoken of his desire to qualify and play for Ireland, and the centre now has two years to make his audition for Andy Farrell. The New Zealand native has agreed a new two-year deal at Munster, which will keep him at Thomond Park until the summer of 2029 at least. It's exactly three years to the day since Nankivell made his debut for the province after joining from the Chiefs, and the centre has been a fan favourite ever since, making 58 appearances in his first three-and-a-bit seasons. With three years in the bank, Nankivell will become Irish-qualified in October 2028. He turns 30 later this week, and so would be a 32-year-old debutant if he does get to earn his shot at Test rugby when the time arrives. And while that still seems like a long way away, the knowledge that he is on course to become Irish-qualified is giving him something to chase.

stories.title: Two-time All-Star Rushe calls time on Dublin career
stories.summary: Two-time Dublin All-Star Liam Rushe has confirmed his retirement from inter-county hurling. The 36-year-old Na Fianna man made a surprise return to the panel last season ahead of the championship, ending a four-year exodus having last played in the 2022 Leinster SHC. He came back into the starting side for Niall Ó Ceallacháin - starting at centre half-back in the Leinster final loss to Galway. Rushe's season came to an end last weekend as Na Fianna lost to Cuala in the Dublin semi-final and on Sunday, he was on punditry duty with TG4 for the Offaly SHC final between Kilcormac-Killoughey and Ballinamere. Following Kilcormac-Killoughgey's 0-19 to 0-17 win, Rushe confirmed he wouldn't be returning to the Dublin squad. "Sin mo rás rite ag an leibhéal idir chontae (that's my race run at county)," said the 2011 Young Hurler of the Year.

stories.title: Saints' title hopes all but ended by impressive Derry
stories.summary: Derry City returned to winning ways thanks to Kevin Dos Santos' second-half header, but in truth, Patrick McClean's defensive display sealed the points against St Patrick's Athletic. McClean - who's older brother James stole all the headlines before the game following his remarks to Paul Kimmage surrounding 'men being weak if they go to therapy' - the former Glentoran centre-back was solid as a rock and produced another player of the match display. The loss for Stephen Kenny's side all but ended their title hopes, as they now sit six points behind champions Shamrock Rovers, with just two games remaining. Derry had a half chance on two minutes as Darragh Burns released Tyler Smith, but the striker's shot from the right hand angle hit the side netting, while at the other end Kian Leavy was denied by a super sliding block by Patrick McClean, after the Saints man had broke in behind the Derry back-line. On 16 minutes the Derry fans showed their disapproval at Ireland international James McClean's recent comments about 'men being weak if they go to therapy' when they unfurled a banner stating 'it's not weak to speak'. Derry missed a good chance just after the mid-way point of the half when Burns and Smith linked up, but the ex-St Pat's man's tame 20 yard strike was saved easily by Joseph Anang. Stephen Kenny made a double change just before the hour mark with David McClelland and Ryan Edmondson replacing Breslin and Aidan Keena.

stories.title: Gibson-Park a doubt as Leinster prepare for Munster clash
stories.summary: Leinster and Ireland scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park remains a doubt for Saturday's BKT United Rugby Championship clash with Munster as he continues recovery from a groin injury. The 34-year-old has not featured in any of the province's first four games of the season, including their Champions Cup opener at the weekend. Assistant coach Tyler Bleyendaal explained that although their star man is back in light training, it is still very much a wait and see situation if he features at the weekend. "Jamison is not training fully, but he is back," the former out-half explained on Monday. "He was back involved today and he did a little bit last week as well, (but) he's really just seeing how he feels at the end of the week, before we make a decision. "He was out there today running around, which is a positive sign I think, but it's one of those ones where it has to be assessed probably a bit closer to the time."

stories.title: Something for the Weekend: Emily Waszak's cultural picks
stories.summary: Emily Waszak is an acclaimed Donegal-based visual artist of Japanese-descent working in sculpture and textiles. With a background in industrial weaving, her work is concerned with ritual, ruin and landscape. Currently showing at the Regional Cultural Centre in Letterkenny, Cailleach Dhubh is Emily's first major solo exhibition in Ireland; it explores widowhood through the lens of the cormorant, (cailleach dhubh), expanding on the artist’s previous work about grief, ritual and landscape. The last film that I saw that made me weep in the cinema (which is what I consider a good time these days) was Hamnet. It was visually stunning and the gaze felt intimate and generous. A beautiful depiction of the importance of making art to work through profound grief. Two films that I have not yet seen, but I am looking forward to watching but have not yet been shown in Ireland are Through a Mirror Darkly, which is a 3-channel film by Naeem Mohaiemen that was shown at Glasgow International earlier this year, and Invisible People, an experimental documentary about Butoh dancing by Alisa Berger. After my husband died, I found it impossible to listen to music. Even songs that I had previously been indifferent to elicited an intense emotional response. It's only in the last couple of years that I’ve been able to enjoy listening to music again, so I feel like I’ve missed a lot of recent releases. For the past couple weeks I’ve been listening to Yuma Abe’s new single, Sore wa Juicy on repeat. I know all the cool kids love Japanese City Pop, but I’m much more into 70’s Japanese folk/rock/psych. Last year when I was in Kyoto I actually got to meet Takashi Matsumoto from Happy End, one of my favourite bands from that era. Major fangirl moment. The last novel I read was Make Strange by Niamh Campbell which I really enjoyed. All her novels are funny and cutting and beautifully written. But in the lead up to an exhibition, I find it difficult to find the time or the focus to handle a whole novel, so I tend to read short stories when I’m in production mode. I’m currently two stories deep into The Diving Pool, by Yoko Ogawa and really liking it so far. Another short story collection I really love is People From My Neighbourhood by Hiromi Kawakami. Not sure if it’s a play or a dance performance or what it is really, but I went to see TANZ by Florentina Holzinger as part of the Dublin Theatre festival and it was intense. To see these amazing bodies pushed to their limits but in complete control was truly fascinating. Still not sure how I felt about it as a work of art, but I would recommend seeing it for yourself. And if you happen to find yourself in Venice at the Biennale this autumn, pop over to the Austrian pavilion to see her other work.

stories.title: Andrew Scott dons two retro-inspired looks in one night
stories.summary: Months into his press run for Elsinore, Andrew Scott isn't slowing down when it comes to both events and stylish outfits to wear to them. The Dubliner has spent the last few months promoting his latest film, a moving biopic about Scottish stage actor Ian Charleson, who took on the role of Hamlet at the National Theatre in 1989 while seriously ill with AIDS. Charleson passed away just two months after his final performance. So far the biopic has been receiving rave reviews for Scott's performance. It was especially meaningful, then, to bring the film to the 2026 NewFest, New York City's largest queer film festival, which took place at SVA Theater last night. For the occasion, Scott stepped out in a bright red leather jacket by Sandro, paired with a matching red t-shirt and black trousers. Styled by Warren Alfie Baker, the look referenced the 80s setting of Elsinore and continued Scott's reputation for a bold red carpet outfit. On the same evening, Scott attended a benefit run by the Golden Heart Awards, a philanthrophic body that honours those who have demonstrated a compassion for the disadvantaged in the Los Angeles community. Last night's event, which took place in New York City, specifically benefitted God's Love We Deliver, a charity that provides medically tailored meals to people living with chronic illness who are not able to feed themselves.

stories.title: Wind and solar power lost due to battery storage issues
stories.summary: Enough renewable electricity to power almost half a million Irish homes was lost during the first nine months of this year because of limitations on the electricity system. New figures from EirGrid show that more than 13% of the wind and solar electricity available in the Republic of Ireland during that period could not be used. The renewable energy industry said the loss highlights the urgent need to accelerate the deployment of large-scale battery storage to capture surplus renewable electricity, reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels and help cut energy bills for consumers. The issue will be highlighted at Ireland's first Renewable Energy Expo, which will open at the RDS in Dublin. The two-day event is jointly organised by Wind Energy Ireland, Solar Ireland and Energy Storage Ireland, bringing the three sectors together for the first time on a shared national platform. Ireland has reached several significant renewable energy milestones, with renewables accounting for half of electricity generation last year and connected solar capacity now exceeding three gigawatts.

stories.title: Rain warnings issued as Storm Austen to hit Ireland
stories.summary: A Status Yellow rain warning has been issued for Ireland on Thursday as the first named storm of the season hits. Met Éireann said heavy rain associated with Storm Austen will spread eastwards across the country. The forecaster said this may lead to difficult travelling conditions and localised flooding, and could impact outdoor events. The warning will be in effect from 7pm on Thursday until 8am on Friday. Met Éireann also said a Status Yellow rain warning will come into effect for Dublin and Wicklow tomorrow. It said the spell of heavy rain could lead to travel disruption and localised flooding.

stories.title: Dáil hears call for 'crackdown' on drug debt intimidation
stories.summary: Sinn Féin has tabled a motion in the Dáil calling for an "immediate and determined crackdown" on drug debt intimidation. Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan thanked Sinn Féin for tabling the motion which he said the Government is supporting. The party's spokesperson on justice, Matt Carthy, introduced the motion during Private Members' Business, urging action to support communities affected by drug-related intimidation. He said that families facing threats and coercion from criminal gangs must receive the protection and support they need - along with "high-visibility policing on their streets". The deputy told the Dáil that families people are living in fear, in despair and "too often feel abandoned". "The horrific murders in Waterford ... shocked us all," he said, adding that TDs must work to ensure such a tragedy never happens again.

stories.title: UK inflation up more than expected on rising fuel costs
stories.summary: Britain's annual inflation rate accelerated by more than expected in September, rising to 3.5% on surging fuel prices, official data showed today. The Consumer Prices Index jumped from an annual rate of 3.1% in August, the Office for National Statistics said. The figures come a week before the UK government's release of its annual budget, which is expected to address cost of living pressures. The September reading was the highest in almost a year, and surpassed analysts' consensus forecast of 3.4%. "Transport, particularly motor fuels, made the largest upward contribution to the change," the ONS said, as the US-Iran war sent petrol and diesel prices soaring. The cost of diesel at UK pumps recently reached the highest level since July 2022, shortly after Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Alberta separatists lose vote on leaving Canada
stories.summary: Alberta residents have voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation, in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid a trade war with the US. CBC News, Canada's government-funded national broadcaster, called the result after 33% of the vote had been counted. At the time of the call, 76% of tallied votes were in support of the "remain" side versus 23% in favour of the province moving forward with a binding vote on separation. The referendum was nonbinding. "Albertans made a clear choice," Mr Carney said in a statement. "They chose unity, to build together, and to take care of each other." Pollsters and analysts had repeatedly dismissed the possibility of a separatist victory, citing data that showed about one-third of residents in the western province supported a future referendum on leaving. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith announced the referendum in May, saying it was "time to have a vote, understand the will of Albertans on this subject, and move on".

stories.title: Rising star Ngumoha relishes bright lights of Anfield
stories.summary: Rio Ngumoha rated his man-of-the-match performance in the 4-3 Champions League victory over Villarreal as one of the best of his relatively short Liverpool career. Alexis Mac Allister may have scored twice but it was the 18-year-old winger who took the plaudits after providing both assists for the Argentina international while giving visiting left-back Sergi Cardona a torrid time. "It's up there with one of the best I've played, I think. I enjoyed myself out there. The team helped me as well a lot. I enjoyed today," he told Prime. After a match-changing substitute appearance at Brentford on Saturday the teenager is starting to become a pivotal figure in head coach Andoni Iraola's game plan. This was his best display for Liverpool as they recovered from 2-0 down after 29 minutes to hold a commanding lead with Ronald Araujo and Florian Wirtz, with his first since April, adding the other goals. "I think he was coming from a very good game the other day, he had a good second half against Brentford," said Iraola.

stories.title: Dublin SFC: O'Callaghan & McMorrow excel in Cuala stroll
stories.summary: Con O'Callaghan netted twice as Cuala returned to the summit of the Dublin SFC, easing to their second title success in three seasons with a rout of outclassed Castleknock. Laying the platform for victory with an unanswered 1-09 in the first half, the 2025 All-Ireland winners surged to another landmark win, the club's second ever title. King Con finished with 2-05 for the Dalkey outfit who trailed briefly early on before hitting the afterburners and burning off a Castleknock side that simply had no response to the onslaught. Jamie Conroy grabbed the other goal for Cuala but that came in the closing minutes of the second half and, in truth, the game as a contest was over at that stage. Dublin duo Eoin Kennedy and Charlie McMorrow contributed two points apiece while even veteran Sky Blues icon Michael Fitzsimons, wearing his usual number three, added a brace of points on a famous day for the club. With the Cuala hurlers also preparing for a senior county final, a dream double of titles remains on the cards.

stories.title: Gonzalez's Finn Harps takeover another step closer
stories.summary: Former Philippines international footballer Freddy Gonzalez has moved a step closer to taking over Finn Harps after one of two votes required to greenlight the acquisition was passed on Monday night. Gonzalez has promised an initial €4m investment into the Donegal outfit if his takeover proposal is passed. The 48-year-old is the co-founder of Terry SA, a retail company in his native country. He has family ties to the International Container Terminal Services, one of the Philippines' most respected business dynasties, which has revenue in the billions each year. On Monday night, a special general meeting of Finn Harps Co-Operative Society Limited was held in Ballybofey. The club's co-op society voted to approve the special resolution for the proposed acquisition. A second vote will now go before members, who must approve the takeover by a 75% majority. "Members of the Finn Harps Co-operative Society voted to approve the Special Resolution for the proposed acquisition of the club by Freddy Gonzalez at a Special General Meeting (SGM) this evening," a Harps statement read. "A second SGM will now be held on Tuesday, 3 November where members will consider and, if thought fit, confirm the same Special Resolution approved at tonight's meeting."

stories.title: Jackman: Lancaster's young stars inspired Connacht win
stories.summary: Former Leinster and Ireland hooker Bernard Jackman has said that Connacht's win over Saracens last Saturday was built on the backbone of Stuart Lancaster's progression of young talent. "I saw Andy Farrell in the crowd in Galway, and he can't not have been impressed with what Connacht put out," Jackman said. "For me it wasn't just the Bundee Akis, the Cian Prendergasts, the Ciarán Frawleys, who were all exceptional, but some of those youngsters (were brilliant). "There's a young hooker there, Matthew Victory, who was a number eight in school, and now he's up against Jamie George, a British and Irish Lions hooker, and holding his own. Finn Treacy from Pres Bray and Thomas Connolly came off the bench for his European debut. "And that's the great thing about (Stuart) Lancaster, the youngster's ability to perform at a high level when they get the chance is outstanding. "That was a huge win to beat Saracens the way they did, having gone 12 points down, up against a team with the kind of power that Saracens had. That has looked like the Achilles heel for Connacht this year.

stories.title: The Waterboys and Gilla Band for Other Voices 25th anniversary
stories.summary: The Waterboys, Gilla Band, Julia Jacklin and Lambrini Girls are among the first six acts announced for the 25th anniversary edition of Other Voices, which takes place in Dingle from 27 to 29 November 2026. The festival will return to St James' Church for its 25th edition, with further performers and details of the wider programme to be announced in the coming weeks. The Waterboys, led by Mike Scott, will return to the venue, where the band will perform alongside Dublin group Gilla Band. The line-up also includes Australian singer-songwriter Julia Jacklin, Brighton punk duo Lambrini Girls, Newcastle jazz collective Knats and Scottish smallpipes musician Brìghde Chaimbeul, from the Isle of Skye. The Jameson Music Trail will also return as part of the festival, with tickets on sale on Friday, 23 October. A limited number of tickets for the church recordings will be made available through competitions, with further details to be announced.

stories.title: Christina Applegate reveals she was misdiagnosed with MS
stories.summary: Christina Applegate has revealed she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) and feels like she is "back at square one". The Anchorman and Dead to Me actress, 54, announced in August 2021 that she had been diagnosed with the autoimmune condition in which the immune system mistakes the body for a foreign substance and attacks it. Applegate said she was in a "state of shock" as she tearfully shared the latest news on her podcast, MeSsY, which she co-hosts with The Sopranos star Jamie-Lynn Sigler, who has MS. The podcast has been a platform for the pair to discuss their journeys living with the condition. Applegate said: "This may come as great news, but to me, I'm back at square one. "It's hard to say that [my doctor] came into my room and she said, 'Congratulations, you don't have MS'. I was not happy at all.

stories.title: Lucy Kennedy: "I think I'm just wired for a crazy life"
stories.summary: As she returns with a new series of Living with Lucy, Lucy Kennedy talks to Claire O'Mahony about her three-minute appraisal of her guests, how she has learned to tolerate people she disagrees with, and how the story for her first novel for adults came to her on a sun lounger. Louis Walsh has frequently told Lucy Kennedy that she is the spit of Noel Fielding, Great British Bake-Off co-host and, given that he has actually met Fielding, she has been forced to concede he may have a point. "Louis and I met and bonded on Ireland’s Got Talent, and every time before I went out live, when I’d be pacing behind the curtain, he’d say, 'Good luck, Noel Fielding.’ He thinks I’m the absolute image of him," she laughs. "I think it’s the hair and maybe the eyebrows." Music manager Walsh is the first guest in the new series of Living with Lucy, returning to Virgin Media on 1 November. The pair headed to Barcelona for a weekend in which their differences quickly became apparent. Kennedy wanted to sunbathe, Walsh hates the sun; she was drinking wine, he doesn’t drink; she wanted to sit down, while he wanted to see the sights. "I had to stop and beg 10 times and say, ‘Louis, we can’t use that,’" she says. "It was such a funny weekend, lots of laughing and lots of good chats, and I was trying to get him to open up and be a little bit more serious with me. I think when he lets you in, he really lets you in." After so many seasons of Living with Lucy, Kennedy, who turned 50 this year, has a fairly reliable sense of how those three days in somebody else’s company will unfold. "I’m like a wasp. I know within the first three minutes," she says.

stories.title: UK government approves drilling in Jackdaw gas field
stories.summary: The UK government has approved plans to begin drilling in the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea. The decision by the North Sea Transition Authority ends months of speculation about the future of the project, which owner Adura said could deliver around 6% of UK North Sea gas production. Britain's Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh, who gave approval for the NSTA to grant consent for drilling, said the move will "support the country's energy security with homegrown gas this winter". Prime Minister Andy Burnham added the decision will "protect hundreds of jobs and help keep millions of homes warm", but stressed it would not hinder the government’s targets on renewable energy. The drilling project is one of two - alongside the Rosebank oil field off Shetland - which were approved by the previous Conservative government. Both were approved for drilling licences in June 2022, but this was overturned by the Scottish courts after a challenge from environmental campaigners.

stories.summary: The Defence Forces said it is not expecting an exodus from the force once the peacekeeping mission in Southern Lebanon comes to an end later this year. This final phase of preparation is known as the Mission Readiness Exercise where troops have to undergo different challenges to prepare for the challenging situations that they could encounter. Different scenarios are set up in the hills of Wicklow so they experience how they will react to a series of risks and how to best protect themselves. Today's exercise included live firing and explosions in the field.

stories.title: Kelly calls for public inquiry into garda gun holsters
stories.summary: Labour TD Alan Kelly has called for a public inquiry into the issue of garda gun holsters and whistleblowers. Mr Kelly said he supports Detective Colm Harkin's family wholly in their quest for answers. Detective Horkan was shot dead by Stephen Silver in Castlerea, Co Roscommon, in June 2020, after Silver took the detective's official firearm from its holster. Concerns have since been raised that the holsters provided to members by An Garda Síochána were not safe or secure, and that Garda management had been warned about related design specification issues before Detective Horkan's murder. Speaking outside Leinster House, Mr Kelly said that the Government's policy is to "deflect, confuse and think that this is going to go away". "This is not going to go away. Full stop. It's not going to go away. We haven't even got through all the issues. Many issues aren't even public," he said.

stories.title: Netflix says 'could do better' after weak forecast
stories.summary: Netflix issued weaker than expected guidance for fourth-quarter profit and cut its full-year advertising forecast, days after the streaming pioneer laid off 6% of its workforce and replaced two of its top programming executives. Shares of Netflix fell nearly 6% to $64.66 in after-hours trading on Wall Street last night. The stock had fallen more than 40% in a year before the earnings report. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos said the company plans to focus on its core business of producing quality TV shows and movies to make Netflix a must-have service, and the recent executive shakeup was a step toward that goal. "I know that we could do better," Sarandos said in a post-earnings video call. "Now we've seen an opportunity to take our slate to the next level." Third-quarter revenue rose 11.8% to $12.87 billion, in line with Wall Street forecasts, but the lowest rate of increase in nearly three years. The company forecast fourth-quarter net income of $2.79 billion and EPS of 67 cents, below the average analyst forecast of $3.07 billion and 73 cents.

stories.title: Irish doctors return from teaching trauma care in Kyiv
stories.summary: Five Irish medical professionals have returned to Ireland from Ukraine after teaching a trauma aid course for first responders in Kyiv last week. The course - the 11th edition organised by the UCD Ukraine Trauma Project since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022 - gave participants a grounding in delivering vital medical aid to trauma casualties. Over the past four years, more than 1,000 Ukrainian first responders have been trained as part of the project, spearheaded by three senior members of the UCD School of Medicine: Emeritus Professor Gerard Bury, Professor Chris Fitzpatrick and Dr Lyudmyla Zakharchenko, all of whom travelled to Kyiv to teach the latest course. Their time in the Ukrainian capital occurred during a period of intensified Russian drone and rocket attacks on the city's energy grid, meaning that some of the classes had to be taught in challenging conditions. "We lost light, heat, internet. The group of trainees are extremely resilient people. They simply took out their torches and continued the work," said Prof Bury. Among last week's 120 participants were combat medics, civilian paramedics, police officers, doctors and nurses, with groups of 30 students being taught the intensive trauma course each day. Many had journeyed from frontline areas.

stories.title: Arteta admits final defeat is still driving him
stories.summary: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta admits the lingering pain of last season's Champions League final defeat is fuelling his desire for European glory and rejected suggestions his team are "boring". The Premier League champions face Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arena thus evening in their biggest test since losing to Paris St Germain on penalties in May. Asked if he had moved on from the agonising shoot-out loss to PSG, Arteta said: "I tried, but I haven’t managed to. "I tried for many weeks during the summer, but when I see the ball, the scenes, I hear the music, I want it so badly. "We know that we have to go step by step, but I think that fire is within the team and all of us individually. "We know what we had to go through – not being champions of Europe by a penalty. So, let’s try again."
